purpose: Defines how a visible research possibility progresses from an idea to usable mature technology, including setbacks, disproven hypotheses, partial success, and side discoveries without turning research into a guaranteed one-click purchase.

investigable.meaning: The civilization has enough knowledge/evidence/applicability to organize a serious program.

experimental.meaning: Experiments/prototypes test whether the proposed mechanism works outside pure theory.

demonstrated.meaning: The underlying principle has been shown to work in a limited or controlled form; some capabilities may become available experimentally.

engineering.meaning: The civilization is turning the demonstrated principle into a reliable manufacturable operational technology.

mature.meaning: The technology is reliable enough to be treated as established civilization knowledge/capability.

established_extension.applies_when: non-hypothesis foundation/developing work with strong prerequisites/evidence
established_extension.description: The underlying science is established; research may run late or produce engineering problems but should not randomly become impossible.

frontier_engineering.applies_when: non-hypothesis advanced/frontier work or weak evidence
frontier_engineering.description: The principle is credible but difficult engineering can cause serious setbacks or hazardous prototypes.

scientific_hypothesis.description: The civilization is testing whether a proposed phenomenon or mechanism is real. Disproof is a valid scientific result, not a wasted campaign action.

hazardous_foreign_or_anomalous.applies_when: explicit node/outcome override marks the project hazardous
hazardous_foreign_or_anomalous.description: Reserved for explicitly dangerous foreign/anomalous work; ordinary research must not inherit disaster risk merely because it is late-game.

progress.effect: Project advances normally toward the next maturity state.

setback.effect: Time/RP is lost to a failed test or engineering problem, but accumulated knowledge is retained.

partial_success.effect: A limited subsystem or reduced-performance implementation works; the project gains evidence/competence and may grant an explicitly configured experimental capability before maturity.

hypothesis_supported.effect: Evidence supports the proposed phenomenon and the project can advance toward demonstration/engineering.

hypothesis_refined.effect: The original model was incomplete; retain scientific progress, improve field competence/evidence, and keep or redirect the research horizon without a total reset.

hypothesis_disproven.effect: The tested version moves to Archived with resolution=disproven. RP is not refunded, but the civilization gains field competence, negative knowledge, and may expose alternative/side possibilities.

hazard_incident.effect: Explicitly hazardous work can damage facilities, personnel, samples, or local infrastructure according to the owning simulation subsystem. The research system records the event/evidence but does not directly simulate casualties/damage.

side_discovery.effect: Unexpected work generates evidence, a hypothesis, field competence, or awareness for another legitimately reachable possibility; it never directly grants an unrelated mature technology.

outcome_inputs: foreign reference material or expert access
previous setbacks on the same project
campaign-seeded deterministic random stream where uncertainty remains

candidate_sources: direct child possibilities of matured/tested knowledge
nodes sharing strongly relevant knowledge fields
alternative solution families for the same recognized problem
evidence-driven candidates newly supported by experiment results
possible_results: reduced uncertainty/cost for an already visible candidate
